I'd love to point to this as 100% proof that Democrats are trying to manipulate public opinion, and it fits in with what we know about them, but here is why it's tough to tell the complete objective truth about this kind of thing.

It's a dirty little secret that few online marketers will admit to in public, but virtually all types of online organizations have experimented with using some kind of bots to manipulate various social media stats or SEO rankings. You don't have to be a large international corporation as even a mom and pop restaurant can set this up. You pay a 3rd party to like posts, like pages, view videos, share links, make random comments, etc. and pump up your online numbers. Even though these aren't genuine customers who buy products, it gives the appearance of popularity and credibility online and can positively impact various sorting and ranking algorithms. Facebook and Twitter and Reddit and all of these platforms are filled with fake users. I know politicians who have done this before and I'm sure that many big political organizations have experimented with this. Hell, there are super-nerds on 4chan who have their own networks of fake accounts who do shit like this for lolz.

That being said, just as it's easy to set this up (literally a tech illiterate small business could figure it out, let alone a big political organization) it's easy to frame somebody as well. Let's say there are political positions A and political position B on some topic. What you could do is hire a 1,000,000 bots to promote position A, and maybe 10,000 bots to promote position B. If you were ever caught manipulating on the side of position A, you could point to the bots that promote position B and declare moral equivalency and wash your hands clean. If you're never caught, when the time is right you could point to position B's bots as proof that your opponent is trying to cheat. And as public observers, it's impossible to prove what really happened because you don't see IP addresses and other data that might give some clues as to who is really behind it. This is so complicated because there could be many groups that are doing manipulation on behalf of position A and position B at the same time.

So really, the only people who are actually in position to make a super educated guess as to what's really going on here (looking at IP addresses, usage patterns, etc) is the social networks themselves, who are politically biased to an extreme and untrustworthy. And if there's a really sophisticated manipulation action going on (either a big political organization with many resources or a state actor) it would be possible to obfuscate where the traffic is coming from anyway.
